messages:
support_eng: Hey team — customer reports intermittent 401s when connecting to the /v1/stream endpoint and occasionally large tail latency (~3s). They provided a curl snippet but our prod logs show different request IDs. Root request id they saw: rq-8f3a2bcd. Can we get a minimal curl repro and a short checklist to collect a debug bundle from their side?

emma: Thanks. Quick checklist to ask the customer for: 1) exact curl command used, 2) full response headers (including x-request-id), 3) raw TCP capture of the SSE handshake if possible, 4) timestamped trace id from our logs. Short and simple please.

jon: I'll draft a minimal curl they can run — needs to reproduce streaming auth handshake only (no app logic). Use http/1.1 and keep-alive. Example to paste and replace values:

```bash
curl -v --no-buffer \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer REPLACE_TOKEN" \
  -H "Accept: text/event-stream" \
  -H "Cookie: signed_session=REPLACE_COOKIE" \
  --http1.1 \
  https://api.redwood.ai/v1/stream
```

jon: Also ask them to run with --trace-ascii to capture headers: `curl --trace-ascii - -v ...` and paste the dump.

infra_oncall: Quick infra checks — if they go through a proxy (corporate gateway) it might terminate keepalive or reuse connections causing auth expiry mid-stream. Ask: are they behind a proxy / VPN / NAT load balancer? Also request the server-side log slice for rq-8f3a2bcd from `api-gateway` and `sse-proxy` between timestamps they saw.

customer_success: I messaged the customer (AcmeCorp) asking for those items. They replied they can run the curl but want a single command that collects headers + body snippet and redacts tokens.

debug-bot: Suggested single-line redaction-friendly command: `curl -sS --no-buffer --http1.1 -H "Authorization: Bearer REDACT_ME" -H "Accept: text/event-stream" -H "Cookie: signed_session=REDACT_ME" --trace-ascii /tmp/trace.txt https://api.redwood.ai/v1/stream` then `head -n 200 /tmp/trace.txt` and paste.

emma: Also ask them to include the OS, curl version (`curl --version`), and whether they used `--http2` or not. If they do use a client library (node/python), ask for the exact lib + version.

jon: If curl trace doesn't show the 401, next step is to capture TLS session reuse: `openssl s_client -connect api.redwood.ai:443 -alpn http/1.1` and compare session IDs before/after. Corporate proxies often terminate TLS and re-sign; that can alter cookies/HMACs.

infra_oncall: I'll pre-collect logs for rq-8f3a2bcd and scan for these patterns: "auth:expired", "cookie:invalid-hmac", and any 502/504 around the same time. If you paste the curl trace we can match the connection flow to our backend trace.

support_eng: Great. Customer posted the trace (redacted) — they ran the one-line command and we can see a 401 at the server handshake. They included `x-client-ip` and `x-forwarded-for`. Next ask: can they run with `--compressed` turned off? Some proxies change content-encoding and break streaming.

customer_success: Customer ran with `--no-buffer` and sent the first 120 lines of trace. They confirm they're behind corporate proxy.

emma: Ok two likely vectors: 1) proxy is stripping/altering cookie or Authorization header on keepalive connection reuse, 2) our signed cookie TTL mismatch with long-lived connections. For a fast mitigation: suggest using short reconnects (client-side) or switching to Authorization header each reconnect instead of relying solely on cookie.

jon: Action items: - customer to run the single-line trace and upload head/tail of /tmp/trace.txt - support to attach api-gateway + sse-proxy logs for rq-8f3a2bcd - infra to search for correlated 401s with same upstream conn id. I'll also prepare a minimal curl that forces a fresh TCP connection per request for testing: `curl -v --no-buffer --http1.1 --no-keepalive -H ...`

infra_oncall: Got it. I'll attach initial logs in this thread once I pull them.

support_eng: Thanks all. Customer said they'll run the no-keepalive test next and paste results. :thumbsup:
